Our method, dubbed the Ensemble Neural Network with Uncertainty-based Selection (ENUS), dynamically selects and combines the predictions of multiple networks based on their confidence levels, effectively mitigating the adverse effects of noisy labels. Our experimental results demonstrate that ENUS outperforms existing methods in both binary and multi-class classification tasks, particularly when dealing with uncertain data. Additionally, we found that ENUS's uncertainty-based selection mechanism enables the identification of noisy data points, which can be utilized for label correction. Our study also reveals that ENUS's performance is highly adaptable to different network architectures and data distributions, making it a versatile solution for real-world applications. However, current metrics have significant drawbacks, such as failing to account for summary diversity and having little correlation with human judgments. To address these issues, we introduce SummScore, a new metric that uses a pre-trained language model to assess summaries by comparing them to a reference using a pre-defined set of semantic and syntactic features. Our results show that SummScore outperforms other metrics in terms of diversity and correlation with human judgments, and we also find that it can be used to improve model performance by incorporating it into the loss function during training. Understanding user intent is crucial for delivering personalized recommendations that meet their needs and enhance their overall experience. However, accurately capturing user intent from implicit feedback is a challenging task due to the lack of explicit intent signals. To address this issue, we propose a novel approach that utilizes a multi-task learning framework to simultaneously predict user intent and item preferences. By leveraging user intent and item features, we develop a neural network that captures intent-related information and incorporates it into the recommendation model. Through this approach, we demonstrate that user intent can be effectively extracted from implicit feedback and utilized to improve recommendation quality. Experimental results on a real-world dataset reveal that our approach surpasses existing methods in both recommendation accuracy and user intent prediction. Moreover, we conduct a user study to validate the effectiveness of our approach and provide insights into the practical applications of user intent in real-world scenarios. Furthermore, we highlight the potential applications of HiTMap in various navigation tasks, such as local mapping, loop closure detection, and obstacle avoidance. subsequently improve the retrieval of relevant entities. Our system, known as

real-time. To achieve this, we employed a Bayesian approach that allows the
system to update its knowledge based on user input. Our evaluation of CEREBA
involved a comprehensive analysis of its performance across multiple domains and
contexts, including both medical and non-medical fields. The results of our
evaluation showed that CEREBA's ability to learn from user feedback significantly
enhanced its performance, with a notable improvement of 25% in retrieval
accuracy. Furthermore, our analysis revealed that CEREBA's ability to adapt to
new contexts in real-time was also a key factor in its improved performance. To

user-friendly interface that enables users to provide feedback and interact with
the system. Our study of CEREBA's deployment in a real-world setting showed

was used by over 1,000 users. The results of our study highlighted the

entity retrieval systems. Our research also demonstrated the potential of CEREBA

Recent advancements in Retrieval Augment Generation (RAG) have shown that pre-trained models can excel in various downstream tasks. However, fine-tuning RAG architectures poses unique challenges due to their dual nature, comprising both retrieval and generation components. This paper investigates the impact of fine-tuning RAG models on their retrieval and generation capabilities, revealing that the two components respond differently to training. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel approach that decouples fine-tuning, allowing for independent optimization of the retrieval and generation components. This method, dubbed RAG-DEC, demonstrates improved performance on multiple tasks and showcases its effectiveness through a series of ablation studies. Notably, RAG-DEC achieves a 4.5% absolute improvement in F1 score on the SQuAD v1.1 benchmark, outperforming the standard fine-tuning approach. This research provides a deeper understanding of the RAG architecture and offers a practical solution to improve its performance in various applications. The growing number of devices in Home WiFi networks is causing congestion, leading to decreased network performance. To address this issue, a novel association mechanism has been proposed that takes into account the load on each channel to optimize device connections. By using a load-aware selection method, the proposed scheme aims to minimize interference and improve overall network performance. To achieve this, a channel load estimation algorithm is employed to determine the current load on each channel, and a load-aware association algorithm is used to select the best access point for each device. The proposed scheme has been evaluated through simulations, which show that it can significantly improve network throughput and delay compared to traditional methods. The results also indicate that the proposed scheme can adapt to changing network conditions and maintain optimal performance. The proposed scheme has been successfully implemented on a Home WiFi network, and the results show that it can improve network performance by up to 30%. The results also show that the proposed scheme can reduce the number of devices that are not associated with an access point by up to 20%.
